description: Native Kubernetes desktop IDE designed for seamless cluster exploration

summary.one_liner: Seabird is a native Kubernetes desktop IDE for the GNOME desktop that lets you explore and manage clusters through a graphical interface.
summary.what_it_does: Seabird is a Kubernetes IDE built for the GNOME desktop. It provides a graphical interface for exploring and managing Kubernetes clusters. The README names a terminal for running commands, monitoring through logs and metrics, and a resource editor that shows the API reference alongside it. Downloads are offered for all platforms through releases, with Flatpak recommended on Linux. Building from source requires GTK4, libadwaita, GtkSourceView 5, VTE and Go, and the project uses go generate to create an embedded resource file before building.
use_cases: manage cluster resources with a GUI
run commands in a terminal against a cluster
edit Kubernetes resources with API reference help
how_to_run: sudo dnf install gtk4-devel gtksourceview5-devel libadwaita-devel gobject-introspection-devel glib2-devel vte291-gtk4-devel golang
sudo apt install libgtk-4-dev libgtksourceview-5-dev libadwaita-1-dev libgirepository1.0-dev libglib2.0-dev-bin libvte-2.91-gtk4-dev golang-go
notable: Built specifically for the GNOME desktop using GTK4 and libadwaita
Integrated terminal for executing commands in the cluster
Resource editor with API reference placed alongside
caveats: README states this is paid software with an unlimited free trial
Designed for the GNOME desktop, so fit on other desktops is not described
Building from source requires several GTK-family development packages
